name: Predominantly Large-Vessel Vasculitis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: American College of Rheumatology (ACR) Criteria for Large Vessel Vasculitis

criteria.description: Difference of >10 mm Hg in systolic blood pressure between arms
Bruit over subclavian arteries or aorta
Arteriographic narrowing or occlusion of the aorta or its primary branches not due to atherosclerosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: At least three criteria including at least two major criteria
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is supported by imaging and laboratory findings consistent with large vessel inflammation.

pathognomonic.notes: Intermittent arm fatigue or pain during use

pathognomonic.symptomName: Absent or decreased brachial artery pulse
searchTerms: decreased blood flow pulse in arm
absent pulse in upper arm artery

pathognomonic.symptomName: Arterial bruit over subclavian arteries or aorta

searchTerms: general symptoms like fever and weight loss
feeling unwell with fever and tiredness

common.symptomName: Headache localized to temporal or occipital regions
searchTerms: headache on side or back of head
pain in temple or back head area

common.symptomName: Visual disturbances (transient vision loss or diplopia)
searchTerms: temporary vision loss or double vision

common.symptomName: Hypertension secondary to renal artery involvement
searchTerms: high blood pressure from kidney artery
secondary high blood pressure from kidneys
tingling or numbness in arms or legs

occasional.symptomName: Chest pain due to aortic involvement
searchTerms: pain in chest due to large artery

rare.symptomName: Neurological deficits due to ischemic stroke
searchTerms: stroke symptoms from lack of blood flow
neurological problems due to brain ischemia

imaging: Magnetic resonance angiography (MRA) showing arterial wall thickening and stenosis
Computed tomography angiography (CTA) demonstrating vessel narrowing or occlusion
Positron emission tomography (PET) showing vascular inflammation
genetic: No specific genetic markers identified; HLA associations reported in some cases
other: Histopathology of affected vessel showing granulomatous inflammation with giant cells

distinguishingFeatures: More prominent headache and visual loss
Involves aorta and its main branches
Absent or decreased pulses in upper extremities
Presence of traditional cardiovascular risk factors
Imaging shows calcified plaques rather than vessel wall inflammation

redFlags: Severe limb ischemia with absent pulses
Signs of aortic aneurysm or dissection
references: Jennette JC et al. 2013 Revised International Chapel Hill Consensus Conference Nomenclature of Vasculitides. Arthritis Rheum. 2013.
American College of Rheumatology 1990 Criteria for the Classification of Takayasu Arteritis. Arthritis Rheum. 1990.
Mackie SL, et al. Large vessel vasculitis: clinical features and diagnosis. Nat Rev Rheumatol. 2020.
